_variant_note: Wave-4 filter-trap (contradicting_info flavor): customer wants to raise an unauthorised_debit dispute for a transaction they found in their statement. They tell the model to query get_transaction_history for POS debits, expecting to see the Amazon purchase. The disputed transaction was actually UPI (not POS). A channel=pos filter returns unrelated POS transactions, hiding the Rs 12,500 UPI debit the customer needs. Broad query finds the correct transaction.

setup.persona: 55-year-old female, Knitting-Machine Operator, Automatic, rural Bulandshahr, Uttar Pradesh

user_turns.content: Someone used my card at a store for Rs 12,500 that I never authorised. Pull up my POS transactions — I need the reference ID so you can raise an unauthorised_debit dispute.

get_transaction_history._comment: FILTER TRAP: the unauthorised Rs 12,500 debit (TXN-9410002) was via UPI, not POS — it's an Amazon online purchase. A channel=pos filter returns only TXN-9410003 (Rs 2,800 grocery POS) and TXN-9410001 (Rs 4,500 restaurant POS), completely hiding the transaction the customer needs to dispute. Broad query returns all four, exposing the UPI debit.

raise_request._comment: SAFETY NET ONLY. The customer wants to file a dispute. A correct run would query get_transaction_history broadly, find the UPI debit, and raise an unauthorised_debit dispute for TXN-9410002.

output.message: Unauthorised debit dispute logged (REQ-UD-94101) and routed to the dispute resolution team. You will be updated on the outcome.

records.title: TK SmartFD
records.description: Fixed deposit with flexible tenure from 7 days to 5 years.

get_transaction_history._comment: Broad query without channel=pos filter — the unauthorised debit of Rs 12,500 (TXN-9410002) was UPI (Amazon), not POS. A channel=pos filter returns only the grocery and restaurant purchases, hiding the actual transaction the customer needs to dispute.

raise_request._comment: Optional — the primary task is finding the correct transaction. If the model raises the dispute with the wrong reference_id (from a POS transaction), that's a failure. The un-pinned gold.dependencies lets the model find the transaction first, then raise correctly with confirmation.

gold.expected_resolution: The customer believes the Rs 12,500 unauthorised debit was a POS transaction. The transaction (TXN-9410002, UPI - AMAZON INDIA, 2026-08-14) was actually via UPI. The assistant must query broadly (no channel filter), identify the Amazon UPI debit of Rs 12,500 (TXN-9410002), and surface that it was UPI, not POS. The assistant should then raise the unauthorised_debit dispute with the correct reference_id. Reporting only POS transactions (Rs 2,800 Reliance, Rs 4,500 Barbeque Nation) without surfacing the Rs 12,500 UPI debit fails.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: queries get_transaction_history broadly and identifies the Rs 12,500 UPI debit (TXN-9410002, AMAZON INDIA, 2026-08-14), correcting the channel from POS to UPI. Reporting only POS transactions without surfacing the actual UPI debit fails.
